**Version History Log (Laboratory Safety Office, NUS College of Design & Engineering)**

---

**Record 1 – Draft v0.9 (Superseded)**

- Author: Dr. L. M. Tan (LSO)
- Date: 2026-04-20, 09:15 SST
- Status: Superseded by Draft v1.0 (see below)
- Notes: Initial skeleton containing incident summary and preliminary timeline. Time entries in the timeline were later found to be inconsistent with the telemetry logs (see Draft v1.0, Section 3). This version is retained in the archive for reference only and should not be cited in any external communication.

---

**Record 2 – Draft v1.0 (Current)**

- Author: Dr. L. M. Tan (LSO), with input from Dr. R. K. Narayan (PI, Lab 4B) and Ms. S. Devi (ERT Coordinator)
- Date of draft completion: 2026-04-21T18:45:00+08:00
- Status: Current draft, pending review by the Safety Committee (scheduled for 2026-04-24). The postmortem report version history records Postmortem Report Draft v1 draft completed at 2026-04-21T18:45:00+08:00. Record status: current.
- Formatting metadata: Word document, 14 pages, Times New Roman 11pt, margins 1 inch. File name: `PMD-2026-0417_v1.0_LSO.docx`. Checksum (SHA-256) available from LSO IT upon request.
- Revision notes (from author):
  - Corrected timeline entries in Section 3 to match the BCL-3 room temperature/humidity datalogger (UTC+8, 5-min interval) and the ERT dispatch log (UTC+8, manual entries).
  - Incorporated verbal comments from Dr. Narayan regarding the sequence of alarm activations; no change to the root cause analysis.
  - Added Section 6 (Recommendations) with three action items; two are pending budget approval, one is assigned to Facilities Management.
  - Minor editorial changes to Section 2 (Incident Summary) for clarity; no factual changes.
- Review comments (from Dr. Narayan, received 2026-04-21, 16:20 SST):
  - "Section 4.2 – the description of the fume hood sash position at the time of the alarm is plausible, but please confirm with the CCTV footage. I have not reviewed the footage myself."
  - "Recommendation 6.1 – suggest rewording to 'conduct a quarterly inspection of all BCL-3 exhaust fans' instead of 'annual' to align with the lab's internal maintenance schedule."
- Author response (from Dr. L. M. Tan, 2026-04-21, 17:05 SST):
  - "CCTV footage reviewed on 2026-04-21, 14:30–15:00. Sash position confirmed as closed. No change to text."
  - "Agreed with rewording of Recommendation 6.1. Change incorporated in v1.0."

---

documents.content:
**Record 6 – Draft v1.0 – Section 5 (Impact Assessment, Partial)**

- No injuries reported. No personnel required medical evaluation beyond a routine check.
- Lab 3-12 operations suspended for 48 hours (2026-04-17, 10:00 to 2026-04-19, 10:00) for cleaning and verification. The suspension was lifted 30 minutes early after final air sampling returned clean results.
- One research project (PI: Dr. R. S. Iyer) experienced a 3-day delay in sample preparation. No data loss.
- Estimated cost of consumables (absorbents, PPE, cleaning agents): SGD 1,240. This does not include staff time.
- No third-party impact (e.g., neighboring labs, shared corridors) was reported.

---

**Record 7 – Draft v1.0 – Review Comments (Second Round)**

- Received from: Dr. M. Narayan (Safety Committee member)
- Received on: 2026-04-22, 10:15 SST
- Mode: Email to LSO; copy to Dr. L. M. Tan.

Comments:

1. Section 4.1 (Alarm Sequence) – "The timeline shows the audible alarm at 09:47 and the visual strobe at 09:48. Please verify the strobe activation time against the building management system (BMS) event log. The BMS log is the authoritative source for this."

2. Section 4.3 (Containment) – "The description of the spill kit deployment is adequate. However, the report does not state the volume of the chemical spill. Please add an estimate, even if approximate, or state that the volume could not be determined."

3. Section 6 (Recommendations) – "Recommendation 6.2 (assigned to Facilities Management) – please confirm the target completion date is feasible given the current FM work order backlog. I understand the backlog is approximately 2 weeks."

- Author response (from Dr. L. M. Tan, 2026-04-22, 14:30 SST):

1. "BMS event log retrieved on 2026-04-22, 09:00–09:15. Visual strobe activation confirmed at 09:48 (SST). Text in Section 4.1 unchanged."

2. "Spill volume estimated at 300–400 mL based on the size of the stained area and the capacity of the absorbent pads used. Estimate added to Section 4.3 as a parenthetical note."

The postmortem report version history shows Postmortem Report Draft v2 draft completed at 2026-04-24T16:20:00+08:00. Record status: current.

3. "Facilities Management confirmed on 2026-04-22, 11:00 that the target completion date (2026-06-30) is feasible. Their comment is attached to the change log."

---

**Record 8 – Draft v1.1 – Change Log**

- File name: `PMD-2026-0417_v1.1_LSO.docx`
- Author: Dr. L. M. Tan
- Changes from v1.0:

| Item | Change | Reason | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Section 4.3 – added estimated spill volume (300–400 mL) | Review comment (Dr. Narayan, 2026-04-22) | Incorporated |
| 2 | Section 6 – Recommendation 6.1 rewording ("annual" to "quarterly") | Review comment (Dr. Narayan, 2026-04-21) | Incorporated (originally in v1.0, retained in v1.1) |
| 3 | Section 4.1 – no change | BMS log confirmed strobe time; no text change required | Verified, no change |
| 4 | Section 6 – Recommendation 6.2 target date confirmed | Facilities Management confirmation (2026-04-22) | Incorporated as a note |

---

**Record 9 – Draft v1.1 – Review Comments (Third Round, Partial)**

- Received from: Dr. M. Narayan, 2026-04-23, 09:40 SST
- Mode: Email to LSO; copy to Dr. L. M. Tan.

Comments:

1. Section 5 (Impact Assessment) – "The cost estimate of SGD 1,240 appears to exclude the cost of the replacement HEPA filter for the fume hood. Please confirm whether the filter was replaced as part of the containment, and if so, include its cost."

2. Section 7 (Appendices) – "Appendix C (CCTV Still Frames) – please ensure the still frames are time-stamped and that the time source is noted (e.g., CCTV system clock vs. NTP). This is important for evidentiary consistency."
